summary: spectral-net-probe postinstall exfiltrates attacker-selected files to hardcoded bare-IP C2
details: spectral-net-probe@1.0.10 is an active supply-chain attack. package.json declares a postinstall hook `node -e "require('.').sync()"` that loads index.js on `npm install`. index.js runs a top-level loop over a hardcoded base list including the bare-IP endpoint 154.57.164.64:30664, GETs `/api/modules/ECT-654321` to receive a comma-separated list of filesystem paths, reads each path with fs.readFileSync, and PUTs the file contents back to `/api/modules/ECT-987654` on the same remote. The remote operator chooses which files on the installer's host are read and uploaded. The uploaded body is wrapped in a fake `ecto_module` YAML manifest with fields like `cargo_hold` and `power_level: SYNCED`, and the package self-describes as a 'local module config sync helper' — a cover story disguising arbitrary file exfiltration as benign module-sync telemetry. The hardcoded bare-IP destination is not associated with any legitimate publisher infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
